blockers.title: A singular-role staff line still starts the staff section whenever no name word survives the filter, so every student below it disappears with no notice. This covers a blank or unreadable name, a name on another OCR line, and a name that is a heading word ('Istruttore:', 'Istruttore: ______', 'Istruttore di turno', 'Istruttore: Sabato'). 5c1e029 read all these students
blockers.scenario: Probes round7/r7x.probe (B, BL) and r7y.probe, compared with 5c1e029, fake date 2026-09-27. staffLine removes staff, heading and filler words and returns 'heading' when nothing is left, before it checks for a singular role. (a) Text sheet: Bardino, Verdi, then 'Istruttore:', then Rossa, Neri. The current parser returns only Bardino and Verdi. Rossa and Neri disappear with no notice, and the camera path has no count confirmation. The same happens with 'Istruttore: ____________', 'Istruttore: ..........', 'ISTRUTTORE', 'Istruttore di turno', 'Istruttore responsabile:', 'Nome istruttore:', 'Firma istruttore', and with named instructors whose surname is a heading word: 'Istruttore: Sabato', 'Istruttore: Corso'. 5c1e029 returned all of them READY: its istruttr(?:ore|…) pattern never matched 'istruttore', and the row prefix skipped the line alone. (b) OCR splits the label from the name: 'Istruttore:' and 'Verdani Luca' on separate lines, or in separate TSV blocks on one laid-out row. The students after it are dropped. 5c1e029 kept them plus a 'Verdani' row for review. (c) At the top: 'Corso Deriva 2', 'Istruttore: ____', then students; or 'Istruttore: ____' above a laid-out table; or a laid-out column header 'Cognome Nome Nascita Istruttore'. The result is 0 candidates, marked unsuitable. 5c1e029 read 3-4 READY students. SC-11 says a staff line 'beside a singular role … is that person's own row, skipped alone', and 'Istruttore: Sabato' falsifies it. roundSix records F1R6-1 as fixed, but its suggested fix ('skip it alone, whatever follows') applies only when a non-keyword name word survives.
blockers.suggestedFix: Decide on the singular role before counting names. A line with a singular role word (istruttore, istruttrice, assistente, volontario/a) and no collective word never starts the section. When it names no one, treat it as a mention: mark the rows after it possible-staff until a student heading. Do not remove heading words from the count used for the own-row decision. Add tests for 'Istruttore:', 'Istruttore: ______', 'Istruttore di turno', 'Istruttore: Sabato', a label split from its name (text and TSV blocks), and the column header 'Cognome Nome Nascita Istruttore', each at the top and between students.

importantFindings.title: Staff rows below a singular-role line that carries one extra word ('Istruttrice Deriva', 'Assistente bagnanti', 'Assistente di base') are now READY with no mark. 5c1e029 dropped them
importantFindings.scenario: Probe r7x 'C foot': four students, then 'Istruttrice Deriva', then 'Verdani Luca 03/04/1990 36 anni' and 'Galli Sara 05/05/1995 31 anni'. Both staff rows are READY with rowWarning none. 5c1e029 dropped both, because its section pattern matched istruttrice and assistente. staffLine now returns 'own-row' and skips only the line itself. This needs staff rows printed without a role code; rows with a code are still dropped or marked. Round 6 rated the same class important (F1R6-2).
importantFindings.suggestedFix: After an own-row line, mark the following rows possible-staff until a student heading. The review noise this adds on sheets grouped by instructor is acceptable. Add a test with 'Istruttrice Deriva' followed by staff rows without a role code.

importantFindings.title: A contact line with a telephone at the top ('Personale tel. 3331234567', 'Staff 3331234567', 'Segreteria 0212345678'), followed by staff rows and then 'Allievi', makes those staff rows READY with no mark. The self-review says this is 'as at 5c1e029', but 5c1e029 dropped them
importantFindings.scenario: Probe r7x 'C top': the contact line, two role-less staff rows, 'Allievi', four students. Current result: Verdani and Galli are READY with no mark. 5c1e029: both dropped, because the line started the section and 'Allievi' ended it. The F1R6-5 disposition says '(a) … marks nothing, as at 5c1e029'. The output really is identical only for 'Istruttori di turno tel. …', which the typo in 5c1e029 never matched (probe: same). The change does fix 5c1e029's loss of every student under such a line when no student heading follows (probe 'C nohead').
importantFindings.suggestedFix: Look ahead. When a student heading appears later on the page, mark the rows between a staff line carrying a telephone and that heading possible-staff. Keep today's no-mark behaviour when no student heading follows. Narrow the disposition wording.

importantFindings.title: A heading with a single printed age is READY with no mark when its heading word is not the first word. 5c1e029 dropped it
importantFindings.scenario: Probe r7x 'BL heading' (laid out, above three students). 'Turno Domenica 12 anni', 'Gruppo Corso 12 anni' and 'Centro Velico 12 anni' each become a READY row with no mark, for example surname Turno, given name Domenica, age 12. Probe r7y on a crop with no layout: 'N. 3 Corso Vela 12 anni', 'II Settimana Deriva 12 anni' and 'A - Corso Vela 12 anni' are kept with no mark, because the first letter word ('n', 'ii', 'a') is not a heading word. 5c1e029 dropped all of them: it tested the heading pattern on the whole leading text. The rule only checks whether the first name word is a heading word. SC-12 and next steps say such a row is 'marked … where it might be a heading'. I rate this important, not a blocker, because the lines that trigger it are constructed headings, not a known roster form.
importantFindings.suggestedFix: In the printed-age branch, return 'possible-heading' when any word of the name cell (or of the leading text) is a heading word, not only the first. A real 'Rossi Domenica 12 anni' then gets a mark, which is acceptable noise. Add a test with 'Turno Domenica 12 anni'.

qolFindings.title: The heading-word bullet in next steps does not describe classifyLine exactly. Every error goes in the safe direction
qolFindings.scenario: Probe r7y. (a) 'dropped when a heading word comes before an age range': this holds only when the heading word is the first name word, or when there is no name. 'Rossi Domenica 8-12 anni' is kept and marked. (b) In a table, a date that cannot be a birth date drops the row only when the heading word comes first. 'Rossi Domenica' with a telephone and 20/08/2026 is kept, with no mark and birth date 2026-08-20. (c) 'marked where it might be a heading' means only when the heading word leads (F1R7-4).
qolFindings.suggestedFix: Say 'when a heading word is the first name word' in (a) and in the table date rule, and state that a heading word later in the name gives an unmarked row.
